content_html_sanitized:
SAN FRANCISCO-
In a great bit of moral grandstanding, the Attorneys General from 22 states issued a letter calling on InLine Classic Cards' President Kingsley Barnham to cease production of the "Classic Hemp" series. The cards with names like "Hashish," "Acapulco Gold" and "Thai Stick" are sold in convenience stores alongside baseball and auto trading cards -- and beer and cigarettes and other all-American products.

"Using slick, full-color cards to glamorize marijuana is an overtly cynical attempt to promote marijuana use to children while turning a profit for yourself," said the letter, written by California Attorney General Dan Lungren, who is running for governor on his record of persecuting sick and dying people who use marijuana. "There are many outrageous and contemptible attempts to promote marijuana use, but efforts targeted at children are particularly loathsome," the letter said.

San Francisco-based InLine introduced the cards in 1994, and stresses that it "is in no way glorifying or encouraging illegal activity of any kind." Perhaps what really offends the AGs is that InLine also says the cards "raise serious questions about basic human rights and freedoms ... (including) the freedom to alter one's consciousness."

In their letter, the Attorneys General asked Barnham to "reconsider your destructive propaganda effort" and drop the cards from production. "It is our hope that you will find the capacity to act responsibly and comply with our request," the letter said.
That should get a few votes and sell lots of cards. Truly, this is a win-win situation. Is this a great country, or what?
